payload.name: Separate speaker-specific feelings during extraction
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when multiple speakers share personal feelings or reactions in a conversation; create separate memories per speaker instead of merging them.
content: During extraction, when one speaker states their own feeling or inspiration and another speaker then shares a different feeling or reaction, create a separate candidate memory for each speaker's self-attributed statement.
Do not merge the second speaker's response into the first speaker's memory; preserve the exact speaker as the subject of each 'I feel' or 'I think' statement.
If a memory candidate aggregates multiple turns, verify that every distinct speaker's claim is represented in its own candidate before deciding to add.

solves: A construction extraction failure occurred when one speaker's feeling was captured but another speaker's contrasting feeling in the same exchange was dropped, leaving later questions about the second speaker unanswerable. The reusable rule is to extract each participant's self-attributed feeling as its own memory during multi-turn conversations, preserving speaker boundaries. This applies to any multi-party dialogue where feelings, preferences, or opinions are exchanged.
